shots.note: opening shot: the whole painting before the first word
'look at the back wall... above the round mirror': the eye is led in to the wall
rise to the Latin line as it is described, then light it and give its reading
'in his own lettering... in that year': settle on the painted year under the signature
'the wife in green is Costanza Trenta': across to her face
'a full year before the date on the wall': back up to the painted 1434, lit
the pull back that ends the cold open: the whole crowded panel and its open question
'drop from the lettering, past the mirror, to the two people': down from the line to the couple

params.title: Was She Already Dead When He Signed the Wall?
params.subtitle: The Arnolfini Portrait · Jan van Eyck, 1434

shots.note: title card
chapter card
'the man on the left, under the dark hat': from the couple up to his face
'most historians take him to be Giovanni Arnolfini': Van Eyck's separate portrait of the same man
the family's move from Lucca to Bruges, each town marked as it is named
Bruges itself, the trading city where the family mixed trade with finance
'now look at the woman in green': across the room to her face
'she married Giovanni': down to the joined hands while her short life is told
'so is this Costanza?': settle on her while her identity is questioned
'begun in her lifetime, finished after her death': from her face across to his
'why would a merchant want a picture like this?': on the merchant himself
a Van Eyck merchant portrait: the status the new merchant class paid for (same panel as before, so no second label)
pull back to the couple at home: one of the earliest such portraits
'the first thing they show us is what they wear': travel down over their clothes
chapter card
'the woman's green dress... gathers its front in her hand': to the gathered skirt
'kept a team of dyers busy for weeks': dyers at work in a Bruges manuscript
the fur lining at her sleeves, then the 2,000 pelts against the usual 600 over that fur
'near the hem, a little blue appears': down to the hem, the blue lit as it is named
'blue was costly and tied to the Virgin Mary': the Virgin's blue mantle
up to the frilled headdress; the thin necklace lit for 'her jewelry is kept modest'
'now cross to Giovanni, in dark plum': across the room to his tabard
'lined with pine marten': down the tabard to its fur hem
'a hundred Russian martens': the figure over the animal counted
'his straw hat, woven in tiny plaits': up to the hat
'his soft boots': down to his feet
'trading silks and luxury fabrics': a patterned Italian silk velvet of the kind he sold
'a walking advert for his business': back on the couple's fabrics side by side
'wealth shown with care': on the woman's measured finery
'laid out openly... the room around them makes the same claim': pull back to the furnished room

params.title: 3. A Room Built to Be Seen

shots.note: chapter card
'the bed behind the couple, hung in deep red': across to the bed
a red-hung bed of the same years in another painter's room: how such beds were shown

overlays.note: the settle is lit while the strip names it (added by the coordinator: the edit request was refused for a dur 0.03 s too long)

shots.note: 'behind the joined hands stands a bench called a settle': down to the bench and its cushion
'carved gargoyles... sit above those hands': up to the small carving, lit
'a carved woman stands on a dragon': up the chair back to the finial, lit
'Saint Martha': the saint with her dragon in a book of hours
'others see Saint Margaret': the other saint who stands on a dragon
'on the floor lies an Anatolian rug': down to the floor, the rug lit and named
'such carpets': a whole Anatolian carpet of the kind painters loved
'beside the mirror hang amber prayer beads': the string lit, then one bead ringed for 'each bead'
across to the window: the round panes lit and named, then the cherry tree beyond
'oranges lie on the sill and chest': down to the fruit, the chest oranges lit
'the single orange on the sill casts a shadow': in close on it, lit
'it is a still life': pull back so the fruit sits in the room like a still life
'above them hangs a gleaming brass chandelier': up to it
'every line here seems to lead the eye to one object, the mirror': down to the mirror
chapter card
'come closer to the round mirror': push in toward the glass, its surface lit
'as costly glass mirrors did then': a painter using a small convex mirror of the period
'a mirror this large could not yet be made': pull back to see its size against the wall
into the reflection: the couple from behind, then the two doorway figures ringed among them
'Giovanni raises his right hand toward them': out of the mirror to his hand
'so who are they?': back into the mirror, as close as the panel allows, on the two visitors
'court painter to Philip the Good, Duke of Burgundy': the duke himself
'the duke paid him... sent him on diplomatic missions': back to the mirror where he may stand
'ten tiny roundels': along the frame, the roundels lit, then the Crucifixion at the top
'the spotless glass itself is read as purity': into the clear surface of the glass
'those after Christ's death... all sit on the woman's side': across to her side of the frame, lit
'why would death and rising gather beside her?': down from the mirror to the woman
chapter card
'the art historian Erwin Panofsky proposed': the man behind the marriage reading
'look at the joined hands at the centre': in to the hands as a vow
'lift your eye to the inscription': up to the line, lit and read as a witness's record
'drop to the lower left': the pattens lit and named, then the second pair farther back
'shoes come off on holy ground': Moses unshod before the burning bush
'his life outside and hers at home', then the love signs named one by one across the room
'the gathered skirt... a fertility pose': in to the gathered skirt
'even the chandelier joins in': up to it, the one lit candle lit
'holding hers tentatively': slow push in on his loose fingers
'at her feet sits a dog': down to the dog
'dogs carved at women's feet on tombs': a tomb brass with the dog at her feet
'his dark clothes may be mourning dress': down over his tabard
'the scenes after Christ's death gather on her side': back to her side of the frame, lit
'she died in childbirth': on the red bed behind her
'both cases rest on the same pair of hands': back to the hands
'neither closes the question': pull back to the couple around their hands
chapter card
'light from the window at left': across to the source of the light
'it glints on the chandelier, the mirror and her headdress': the band where all three catch it
'many thin, see-through layers called glazes': close on the green where the colour deepens
'smooth and luminous': slow move over the smooth wall to the mirror glass
wet into wet and a dry brush: from the fur trim across to the dog's coat
'they called him an alchemist': the painter, probably by his own hand
'only some twenty-three paintings': the figure over another of his panels
'symbols for us to hunt... like these amber beads': across the wall to the beads, lit
'look back at the woman in green, in that same light': across to her
'lift your eye once more to the line above the mirror': the signature lit one last time
'the hands, the shoes and the fruit can speak of a marriage': each named over the band that holds them
'the dog, the dark clothes': down to the dog by his tabard
'the scenes on her side can speak of a loss': up to her side of the mirror frame, lit
'the hinge is the woman': slow push in on her face
'his work was sought after': up to the mirror, the detail later painters took from him
'Velázquez among them in Las Meninas': his mirror beside the one on Velázquez's back wall
the last shot: from the two figures in the mirror back to the whole painting
